clue.text: Ostentatious display of spectator refreshments at sporting event?

parts.note: a fan is a supporter watching a game
fare is food and drink provided, here imagined on sale at the ground

explanation.surface: A grand show put on with the snacks sold to spectators at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: a fan's fare would be the refreshments a spectator buys.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish of trumpets, and by extension any showy display or fuss, is called this.

clue.text: Little weight behind American news report

indicators.note: in this down clue the weight is placed after, below, the other pieces

parts.note: N stands for new, so news is taken as two of them, NN
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A small item of American news being reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as N plus N, the plural of N for new.
explanation.definitionFit: To report something is to declare or proclaim it publicly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Principal way of working cutting wood

indicators.note: the method phrase slices into the wood, sitting inside it

parts.note: a forest is a large wood
MO, modus operandi, is a method of operating

explanation.surface: The main method used for felling trees in a woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal as an adjective means first in rank or importance, a synonym.

clue.text: Like a certain jacket, maybe label that Hannah has?

definitions.meaning: some jackets can be worn either side out
the name Hannah reads the same backwards, so the label one might give her name is that it can be turned around

explanation.surface: Wondering what tag Hannah's coat carries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'label' points not to a clothing tag but to a description of the name Hannah, which is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket wearable inside out, and a palindromic name, can both be turned around and still work.

clue.text: Picked up beloved animal

indicators.note: picked up as heard, the way a radio picks up a signal, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: dear means much loved

explanation.surface: Collecting a much-loved pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag or doe is an example of the animal named; the definition is a general class.

clue.text: Round figure recorded every so often playing cricket?

definitions.text: recorded every so often playing cricket?
definitions.meaning: a batsman out without scoring has zero entered against his name, which happens often enough

explanation.surface: A tally of something noted at intervals during a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter dismissed without scoring has a zero entered in the scorebook, known as a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is written as a circle, so it is literally a round numeral.

clue.text: British family covering up each burglary

indicators.note: in this down clue the relatives sit under the other pieces, holding them up from below

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A British household hushing something up about each burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: A forced entry into a building to steal is a burglary; the hyphenated noun names the same crime.

clue.text: Scrap, initially overlooked, vet gives for recycling

indicators.note: recycling remakes material into something new, so these letters are reworked
the opening letter of the word vet is ignored, leaving ET

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vet handing over a scrap for the recycling bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially overlooked' drops V from vet, leaving ET; 'for recycling' rearranges ET plus GIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace or tiny remnant of something is a scrap, a synonym.

clue.text: Resort area discovered on voyage

indicators.note: dis-covered: the word area loses its covering letters at both ends

parts.note: a course is the route of a journey, here the voyage

explanation.surface: A holiday spot found while travelling at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' means uncovered: AREA without its outer letters gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Recourse means a fallback one turns to, the noun sense of resort in 'last resort'.

clue.text: Deeply impress European with northern accent

parts.note: the grave is an accent mark, as in à

explanation.surface: A European speaking with a northern accent who makes a strong impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accent' is not a manner of speech but the written mark called a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave something on the mind is figuratively to fix it there permanently.

clue.text: Expecting Portugal to introduce ruling

indicators.note: the country's letter goes first, leading in the other piece

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
regnant means reigning

explanation.surface: Anticipating that Portugal will bring in a new rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is a euphemism for carrying a baby.

clue.text: Sue starts to party early, imbibing wine with Nick

indicators.note: drinking in, so the two first letters hold the other pieces
the first letters of party and early are taken

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine
a nick is a small cut

explanation.surface: A woman called Sue arriving early at a party, drinking wine with a man named Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a name but is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To take legal action against someone is to sue them in court.

clue.text: Bird identified by some beautiful markings

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird recognised by its attractive plumage patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Bird identified' is narrowed to 'Bird': 'identified by' is the link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fulmar is a grey and white seabird of the petrel family, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Cheaply produced lace?

definitions.meaning: made on a very small budget, as in a low-budget film

explanation.definitionFit: Something done on a tiny budget is described this way, and a shoelace is literally such a string.

clue.text: Superficial knowledge of subject Carol possesses

indicators.note: the verb for singing holds the topic inside it

parts.note: to carol is to sing
subject matter, the topic, is matter

explanation.surface: A woman called Carol has only a slight grasp of a topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a name but is the verb meaning to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight, scattered acquaintance with a subject is called a smattering.

clue.text: Plays cards, requiring time for conclusion of game

indicators.note: the cards need the time letter in place of another, a replacement

parts.note: aces are high playing cards

indicators.note: the final letter of game is taken

explanation.surface: Someone playing cards, with the game needing time to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' marks the swap: T goes in for E, the last letter of game.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical works or parts of a show, and performances, are acts; plays as a verb also means acts.

clue.text: Food seasoning at intervals usually going into flattish cake

indicators.note: the picked letters are put inside the cake

parts.note: a tablet is a small flat block, as of soap or a confection

indicators.note: every other letter of usually is taken

explanation.surface: Seasoning normally put into a flat cake at regular points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' takes the even letters of usually, SAL, which go into TABLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary salt used at the dinner table is the commonest food seasoning.

clue.text: Oriental is managing to maintain charm

indicators.note: the words maintain, hold within them, the run of letters wanted

explanation.surface: An Eastern figure is coping with keeping an appeal going.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to bring luck, a lucky charm.

clue.text: Exposed groups of players, those regarded as rejects

parts.note: out means revealed, out in the open
a cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Acting troupes exposed and seen as failures.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcasts are people rejected by society, regarded as pariahs.

clue.text: Student wearing Australian mate's gear

indicators.note: the friend wears the student, holding that letter inside

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a friend; the 's here reads as is
L for learner, from the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student dressed in the clothes of an Australian friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for clothing or kit, so it means gear.

clue.text: Tense son traded securities

parts.note: the future is a verb tense
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An anxious son selling his shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous but is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: Futures are contracts to buy or sell at a set later date, exchanged on markets.

clue.text: Touch musical instrument all over

indicators.note: turned over completely, so the instrument's name is read backwards

parts.note: the tuba is a large brass instrument

explanation.surface: Fingering a musical instrument everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that adjoin or border each other touch, as neighbouring plots do.

clue.text: Waste time attending clubs, perhaps in formal wear

parts.note: to lounge is to idle about
clubs is one example of a card suit

explanation.surface: Idling around at nightclubs, maybe dressed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests nightclubs; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's matching jacket and trousers for business or semi-formal occasions is formal dress.

clue.text: Frightful girl is silly from time to time

indicators.note: only some letters, every other one, are picked from the words

explanation.surface: A girl who sometimes behaves foolishly is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisly means gruesome or causing horror, so it is a synonym for frightful.

clue.text: Show court information that must free murderer essentially

indicators.note: the letters are let go, released from the court word

parts.note: evidence is what a court hears

indicators.note: the essence, the central letters, of murderer

explanation.surface: A display of courtroom proof that may let a killer walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' gives DE, the middle of murderer; freeing it from EVIDENCE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to reveal or display it, a synonym of show.

clue.text: Reportedly express disapproval of furniture material in shop

indicators.note: as reported by speech, so the words are said and heard

parts.note: boo, a jeer, and teak, a hardwood used for furniture

explanation.surface: Someone tutting at the wood used for furniture in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small fashionable store, a kind of shop.

clue.text: Peacekeepers on somewhat empty Shetland island

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: emptied of its inside, leaving only the outer letters of somewhat

explanation.surface: UN troops arriving on a fairly deserted island in Shetland.
explanation.definitionFit: Unst is the most northerly inhabited island of the Shetland group, off Scotland.

clue.text: Around an hour after midnight, sees stray cat

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the time
a stray wanders, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: one in the morning, written 1 a.m. and read as I AM

explanation.surface: Late at night someone spots a stray moggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an hour after midnight' is 1 a.m., with the numeral 1 read as the letter I; 'stray' scrambles sees around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of cat with blue eyes and a pale coat.

clue.text: I heard ultimately charming young woman supplies optical equipment

indicators.note: the word is taken as heard, by its sound

parts.note: the pronoun I, spoken, is the word for the organ of sight

indicators.note: the very end letter of charming

parts.note: lass is a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: I gather a delightful girl provides glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle or lens for aiding sight is optical equipment.

clue.text: Worry easing somehow surrounding Leader of Opposition

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the initial
done some way or other, so these letters are rearranged
the first letter of Opposition

explanation.surface: Concern relaxing in some way around the head of the Opposition party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges EASING to AG...NISE, which surrounds O.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise over something is to fret and suffer anxiety about it.
